title: Shortest Block With the Same Degree

concept.title: Count, first position and last position of every value
body: The **degree** of an array is the largest number of times any single value occurs. You look for the shortest block of consecutive elements that has the same degree as the whole array. Such a block must contain all copies of a value that reaches the degree, and it is shortest if it starts at the **first** copy and ends at the **last** copy of that value.

body.code:
first, last, count = {}, {}, {}
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    first.setdefault(x, i)
    last[x] = i
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
degree = max(count.values())
best = min(last[x] - first[x] + 1 for x in count if count[x] == degree)

body: Three maps (count, first position, last position) are filled in one pass. If several values reach the degree, the best block is the shortest one among them.

statement: The degree of an array is the largest number of times any value occurs in it. Find the length of the shortest block of consecutive elements that has the same degree as the whole array.
outputFormat: Print the length of the shortest block.

examples.note: The degree is 2 (the values 1 and 2). The block 2 2 has length 2.

hints: Find the degree: the largest count of any value.
For a value with that count, the shortest block runs from its first to its last position.
Keep the smallest length over all such values.
